# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 41 (Bi-Vb Pc41)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc41
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 41
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 41. Visiting places of pleasure
**Title (English, from literature):** Visiting places of pleasure
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-pc41
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rājāgāra-sikkhāpada* ("Visiting places of pleasure", Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 41) establishes a rule of expiation (*pācittiya*) for any nun who goes to view recreational or leisure sites [Roth 1997; SuttaCentral]. The promulgated rule stipulates that an offense of expiation is committed if a nun goes to see a king's pleasure house (*rājāgāra*), a picture gallery (*cittāgāra*), a park (*ārāma*), a pleasure grove (*uyyāna*), or a lotus pond (*pokkharaṇī*) [Roth 1997]. In the rule's origin narrative, the group of six nuns visits a picture gallery inside a pleasure park (*uyyāne cittāgāre*), although the formal precept was formulated to encompass the wider list of pleasure grounds [Hüsken 1997]. Hüsken notes that this rule serves as a specific monastic restraint for nuns regarding contemporary worldly amusements and lacks a direct counterpart in the Bhikkhu Vinaya [Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (Pc 41) and Bhikkhunī Parivāra (Pc 41), along with Chinese Vinaya parallels in the Dharmaguptaka (Bi Vb Pc 100 and Prātimokkha Pc 100), Mahīśāsaka (Bi Vb Pc 99 and Prātimokkha Pc 99), and Sarvāstivāda (Bi Vb Pc 99 and Prātimokkha Pc 99) traditions [SuttaCentral]. In Pali-internal text reuse, DharmaNexus identifies shared formulaic passages across 75 other Vinaya texts, showing its largest correspondences with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 10, Pācittiya 50, Pācittiya 42, Nissaggiya Pācittiya 6, and Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 50 [DharmaNexus]. An English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
